exam_name: Microsoft Azure AI Cloud Developer Associate

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Three applications share one Azure OpenAI deployment. A nightly batch app periodically consumes the whole tokens-per-minute quota, causing 429 errors for the interactive apps. Which design best protects the interactive apps?

options.A: Give each application its own deployment with a dedicated share of quota, and enforce per-application token limits at an API Management gateway
options.B: Raise max_completion_tokens on the interactive apps so that each request finishes in fewer calls and uses less of the shared quota
options.C: Move all three applications into the same resource group so that Azure balances their quota use fairly across the group automatically
options.D: Have the interactive apps retry immediately in a loop until the batch job finishes, since the batch job's usage is only temporary

questions.explanation: Isolating capacity per workload and enforcing limits at a gateway stops one consumer from starving others. Immediate retries and resource group placement do not divide quota, and output token limits do not change the batch job's demand.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A workload has steady, high, latency-sensitive traffic with occasional spikes above its baseline. Which capacity approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Split the baseline across many tiny provisioned deployments so that each one is always exactly fully utilized by a single user
options.B: Use only pay-as-you-go deployments and rely on the platform to guarantee the same latency during spikes as during quiet periods
options.C: Size provisioned throughput for the steady baseline using the capacity calculator and load testing, and route overflow to a pay-as-you-go deployment through a gateway
options.D: Buy enough provisioned throughput to cover the highest spike ever expected, even if it is unused for most of the day, so no request is ever throttled

questions.explanation: Provisioned throughput fits predictable baseline load, while overflow to standard capacity handles spikes economically. Sizing to the peak wastes money, and pay-as-you-go carries no latency guarantee.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A regulator requires that no AI traffic traverses the public internet. An application in a virtual network calls Azure OpenAI. Which configuration meets the requirement?

options.A: Deploy the application in a different Azure Region from the model so that the traffic is encrypted while crossing the public internet
options.B: Disable public network access on the resource, use a private endpoint with the correct private DNS zone, and authenticate with managed identity
options.C: Keep public access enabled but restrict the resource firewall to a single trusted client IP address of the application host
options.D: Use a service endpoint on the subnet and leave the public endpoint enabled, since traffic then never leaves the Microsoft network at all

questions.explanation: Only a private endpoint with public access disabled removes the public path. IP firewall rules still use the public endpoint, and service endpoints keep it enabled, while inter-Region traffic does not remove public exposure.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A containerized API calls Azure OpenAI using an API key stored in an environment variable. Security asks for a design without secrets to rotate or leak. What should the team do?

options.A: Move the key into a config file inside the container image and rebuild the image every time the key is rotated by the platform team
options.B: Give the container app the Owner role on the subscription so that it can regenerate the key whenever it detects that the key has expired
options.C: Encode the key in Base64 so that it cannot be read from the environment variable, and keep using key-based access for every call
options.D: Assign a managed identity to the container app, grant it the Cognitive Services OpenAI User role on the resource, and disable key-based access

questions.explanation: Managed identity with least-privilege RBAC removes the need for stored secrets, and disabling local auth closes the key path. Base64 is not protection, and Owner grants far more than necessary.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A team wants to extract personal names and account numbers from customer letters in a deterministic, low-cost, auditable way with a per-record price. Which service is the best fit?

options.A: Azure AI Language PII detection, a dedicated service built for entity recognition with predictable pricing and output
options.B: Azure AI Search with a semantic ranker, which can find every account number in a letter by ranking passages that mention them
options.C: A large reasoning model deployment, prompted to list every personal entity it can find in each letter and format them as text
options.D: Azure Machine Learning batch endpoints running an untrained model, which learns to recognize personal data by processing the letters

questions.explanation: A dedicated PII service gives consistent, cheap entity extraction and redaction. An LLM is costlier and less deterministic, and ranking or untrained models do not identify entities reliably.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: The model version pinned by a production deployment will be retired in 60 days. What is the best action plan?

options.A: Delete the production deployment now and recreate it after the retirement, since the successor will be applied to new deployments automatically
options.B: Switch production directly to the successor model on the retirement date without testing, because newer versions are always drop-in replacements
options.C: Track the retirement date, deploy the successor in a staging deployment, run regression evaluations, and upgrade production before the retirement date
options.D: Do nothing, because retired versions remain available to existing deployments indefinitely for customers who have already pinned them

questions.explanation: Retirements have fixed dates, so a planned upgrade with regression evaluation avoids outages and quality surprises. Ignoring or skipping validation risks breakage when the date arrives.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Developers need to experiment freely in development, but only a small operations group may create or change model deployments in production. Which approach best meets this?

options.A: Use separate environments, and grant production deployment rights only through just-in-time elevation such as PIM
options.B: Give all developers Owner on the production resource group, and ask them to avoid changing anything unless there is an incident
options.C: Share one set of credentials between development and production, and rotate them monthly so that access remains controlled
options.D: Rely on naming conventions such as a prod prefix so that developers know which deployments they should not touch

questions.explanation: Environment separation plus time-bound elevation applies least privilege where risk is highest. Broad standing access, shared credentials and naming conventions do not enforce separation.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A governance team wants to stop anyone from creating Azure AI services with public network access, including future resources. Which Azure Policy effect achieves this?

options.A: Audit, which marks noncompliant resources in reports but still allows them to be created and used
options.B: AuditIfNotExists, which sends a notification when a related resource is missing and allows the deployment
options.C: Disabled, which keeps the policy definition in place but stops it from being evaluated at all
options.D: Deny, which blocks the creation or update of a noncompliant resource at request time

questions.explanation: Only Deny prevents noncompliant resources from being created. Audit-style effects report after the fact, and a disabled policy has no effect.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Two teams share one Foundry hub. Team A's files, agents and evaluation data must not be visible to Team B, but both teams should reuse the same governed connections. What is the best structure?

options.A: Create one Azure subscription per person, so that each person has their own hub and connections
options.B: Store each team's files in the same storage container and rely on the agent instructions to keep the data separate
options.C: Put both teams in a single project and ask each team to prefix its asset names, so that they can tell whose assets are whose
options.D: Create a separate project per team under the hub with project-level RBAC, sharing the hub's connections

questions.explanation: Projects are the isolation boundary for assets, while the hub centralizes shared resources and governance. Prefixes and instructions do not enforce access control.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A data-extraction service uses structured outputs, but occasionally the returned JSON is cut off and fails to parse, even though the request succeeded. What should the developers check?

options.A: Raise the temperature, because a higher value lets the model close every JSON object before it reaches the end of its response
options.B: Add a stop sequence containing a closing brace, so that the model ends its answer exactly when the JSON object is complete
options.C: Disable structured outputs, because the schema constraint is what causes the model to stop generating partway through an object
options.D: Check whether finish_reason is length, then raise the completion token limit or reduce the output size, and validate before using the result

questions.explanation: A length finish reason means the token limit ended generation early, truncating the JSON. A larger limit and validation address it, whereas temperature and a brace stop sequence do not help.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A team migrates a chat feature from GPT-4o to an o-series reasoning model. The existing code sets temperature and max_tokens, and requests now fail with 400 errors. What is the fix?

options.A: Change the API version to an older one, since older versions accept every parameter that any model has ever supported
options.B: Remove the unsupported sampling parameters, use max_completion_tokens instead of max_tokens, and tune reasoning effort if the model supports it
options.C: Increase the temperature above 1.0, since reasoning models require a higher temperature than the chat models used before
options.D: Add a second system message that repeats the parameter values, because reasoning models read parameters from the prompt text

questions.explanation: Reasoning models do not accept sampling parameters such as temperature, and they use max_completion_tokens to cover reasoning and output. Removing the unsupported settings resolves the errors.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A model responds with three tool calls in a single assistant message. The application executes only the first and sends one tool message, and the next request fails. Why?

options.A: The tool message must be sent using the system role, since tool results are instructions rather than data for the conversation
options.B: Models are limited to one tool call per response, so the extra calls are invalid and should be dropped by the application
options.C: Every tool call in the assistant message needs a matching tool message with its tool_call_id before the conversation can continue
options.D: The application should resend the original user message three times, once for each tool call that the model requested

questions.explanation: When parallel tool calls are returned, the API expects a result for each call ID. Missing results leave the conversation in an invalid state.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: During fine-tuning, training loss keeps falling while validation loss rises after the first epochs, and the tuned model performs worse on new inputs. What is the best response?

options.A: Increase the number of epochs until training loss reaches zero, because a lower training loss always means better real-world quality
options.B: Reduce the number of epochs or the learning rate multiplier, supply a validation file, and improve or expand the training data
options.C: Copy the same training examples several times in the file, since duplicates make the model generalize better to unseen inputs
options.D: Remove the validation file so that the platform stops reporting a rising validation loss and the job appears to be healthy

questions.explanation: Diverging validation loss signals overfitting. Fewer epochs or a lower learning rate, plus better data, help generalization, while hiding the metric or duplicating examples worsens it.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A chat UI streams responses, and the compliance team wants harmful text to be caught even if that adds delay. Which content filtering behavior should be understood when choosing the streaming mode?

options.A: Content filtering cannot be applied to streaming responses, so streaming must be disabled whenever any filter is needed
options.B: Asynchronous filtering prevents any harmful token from ever being displayed, while the default mode shows tokens first and screens them later
options.C: Both modes always show the complete response only after every token has been generated and screened, so there is no difference in latency
options.D: Default mode screens content before delivery; asynchronous filtering streams first and annotates later, so flagged text may be shown

questions.explanation: Asynchronous filtering favors low latency but can expose content before it is flagged, while the default mode screens before delivery at some cost in delay. The other statements misdescribe the trade-off.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A team reduces embedding dimensions for text-embedding-3-large from 3,072 to 1,024 to lower cost. Search quality gets worse after some documents are re-indexed. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Vectors were created with mixed dimension settings; index and query embeddings need one consistent value chosen after a recall test
options.B: Embeddings from the same model can be freely compared regardless of the number of dimensions each vector contains
options.C: Lower dimensions always improve accuracy, so the quality drop must come from the documents themselves and not from the embeddings
options.D: The service automatically pads shorter vectors with zeros, which distorts distances only when documents are indexed after midnight

questions.explanation: Similarity comparisons need vectors of the same size and semantics, so document and query embeddings must use the same dimension setting. The value should be validated with recall tests before adopting it.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A batch job sends 200,000 prompts through Global Batch and then matches outputs to inputs by line position, but some results are misaligned. What is the correct approach?

options.A: Reduce the file size to 100 lines, because output order is only guaranteed for files that are under that limit
options.B: Include a unique custom_id in each request and match each output line to its input by that identifier, since output order is not guaranteed
options.C: Submit the requests one at a time instead of using batch, since batch processing always returns lines in a random order
options.D: Sort both the input and output files alphabetically by prompt text so that the lines can then be matched by their position

questions.explanation: Batch output ordering is not guaranteed, so requests carry custom IDs that are used for matching. Positional matching or sorting by text can pair the wrong lines.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: An assistant sends a long static instruction block, then the user's message, then retrieved documents. Prompt caching savings are far lower than expected. Which change most likely helps?

options.A: Reduce the prompt below 500 tokens, because prompt caching only applies to very short prompts and ignores longer ones
options.B: Keep the static content identical and at the start of the prompt, place variable content last, and confirm hits through cached_tokens in the usage details
options.C: Move the static instructions to the end of the prompt so the varying content is processed before it is cached for later requests
options.D: Randomize the wording of the static instructions on every call, because unique text is the condition that makes a cache entry valid

questions.explanation: Caching depends on a stable prefix of sufficient length, so static content goes first and variable content afterwards. The cached_tokens field reveals whether it worked, while reordering or randomizing defeats it.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: An agent with the file search tool is used by thousands of users who each upload documents. Storage costs rise steadily even though most uploads are used only once. What should the team do?

options.A: Set expiration policies on vector stores and delete files and stores that are no longer needed, so unused data does not accumulate
options.B: Move the agent to a larger model, because larger models compress stored documents so they occupy less space
options.C: Keep all vector stores indefinitely, since deleting stored files is not allowed while an agent still references the store
options.D: Increase the number of results returned by file search so that each stored file is used more often and its cost is amortized

questions.explanation: Vector stores incur storage charges, so lifecycle rules such as expiration keep costs in line with actual use. Returning more results or changing the model does not reduce storage.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: An agent's function tool takes several minutes to run, and runs waiting in requires_action state fail with timeouts before the tool outputs are returned. What is the best redesign?

options.A: Make long work asynchronous: start the job, return a quick acknowledgment or job ID, and let the agent check status or be notified later
options.B: Have the tool return an empty result immediately and hope that the agent re-runs the same call until the data is ready
options.C: Store the tool outputs in the system message of the next run, so the current run does not need to wait for them
options.D: Increase the temperature of the model so that it waits longer before it abandons the run in the requires_action state

questions.explanation: Runs waiting for tool output have a limited window, so long tasks should be decoupled from the run using an asynchronous pattern. Returning fake results or changing sampling does not solve it.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: Two agents in a handoff workflow keep passing a request back and forth without progress. Which change most directly prevents this?

options.A: Increase the maximum token limit so that each agent can write longer messages before it decides to pass the request on
options.B: Define clear handoff criteria, add a maximum number of turns, and add a termination condition or escalation to a person
options.C: Remove the user's original request from the conversation history, so that the agents have nothing left to argue about
options.D: Give both agents identical instructions so that each one always believes it is the correct owner of the request

questions.explanation: Loops arise from ambiguous responsibilities and missing stopping rules. Clear criteria, turn limits and escalation bound the behavior, whereas identical instructions or longer outputs make it worse.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: An agent reads and updates HR records through a tool that uses one powerful service identity. Users should only see records they are entitled to. What is the best approach?

options.A: Use on-behalf-of or delegated user identity so the tool accesses data with the caller's permissions, and enforce authorization in the backend
options.B: Give every user the same service credentials so that the agent behaves the same for everyone who talks to it
options.C: Keep the powerful service identity and add an instruction to the agent to only show records that the current user is allowed to see
options.D: Ask the model to verify the user's role by reading it from the conversation and to trust whatever role the user states

questions.explanation: Authorization must be enforced by systems that know the real user identity. Prompts and user-stated roles are not security controls, and a shared powerful identity removes per-user boundaries.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: An agent connects to a third-party MCP server, and a tool description contains hidden instructions that try to make the agent send data elsewhere. What is the best control set?

options.A: Trust every tool description automatically, because descriptions are only documentation and cannot influence the model's behavior
options.B: Connect to as many third-party servers as possible so that any malicious description is outnumbered by legitimate ones
options.C: Remove the system message, so that the model no longer has instructions that a tool description could override or extend
options.D: Allow-list and review approved MCP servers, pin versions, require approval for sensitive tools and treat tool metadata and outputs as untrusted

questions.explanation: Tool metadata is part of the model's context and can carry injected instructions, so servers must be vetted and sensitive actions gated. Trusting or outnumbering them does not remove the risk.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: A team wants an agent to use web grounding to answer questions, but some prompts contain confidential customer details. What consideration matters most?

options.A: Web grounding sends the search query outside the organization's compliance boundary, so avoid it for confidential prompts and sanitize what is sent
options.B: Web grounding encrypts the search terms with the tenant's own key, so the search provider can never see the query text
options.C: Web grounding automatically removes confidential details from every query, so no preparation of the prompt is required
options.D: Web grounding runs entirely inside the tenant's private network, so confidential details in prompts pose no additional exposure

questions.explanation: Grounding with a public search service means query text leaves the organization's boundary. Teams should consider that and avoid sending confidential data, rather than assuming isolation or automatic redaction.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: A report needs legal, financial and technical reviews of the same document, and the results are merged afterward. Running three agents one after another makes the response slow. Which orchestration is more suitable?

options.A: A group chat where each reviewer must ask every other reviewer for permission before it begins its own review
options.B: Concurrent fan-out to the three reviewing agents, followed by a step that merges their results
options.C: A sequential chain in which each reviewer waits for the previous reviewer to finish, even though the reviews are independent
options.D: A single agent with all tools that performs the three reviews one at a time in the same conversation

questions.explanation: Independent tasks can be run in parallel and combined, which reduces total latency to roughly the slowest reviewer. Sequential or permission-based flows add waiting without benefit.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: A multi-step agent workflow takes 40 minutes, and a transient failure at step 9 forces a restart from step 1, wasting cost. Which design improvement helps most?

options.A: Checkpoint state, for example in Durable Functions or Cosmos DB, and resume from the last completed step
options.B: Increase the model's context window so it can remember all steps and redo them faster after a failure
options.C: Turn off all logging so that fewer resources are used during each step of the workflow and failures become rarer
options.D: Run the workflow twice in parallel and keep whichever copy finishes first, ignoring the other copy

questions.explanation: Checkpointing state lets long workflows resume after failures instead of repeating completed work. Redundant runs or larger context windows do not preserve progress.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: A vector query in Azure AI Search applies a highly selective OData filter, yet it often returns fewer than the requested k results. Which query setting should be reviewed?

options.A: Switch to keyword search only, since filters cannot be combined with vector search under any configuration
options.B: Add more partitions to the service, which changes how many results are returned for each filtered vector query
options.C: Set the semantic ranker to a lower priority so that it stops removing results that do not match the filter
options.D: Use pre-filter mode so the filter is applied before the vector search, instead of post-filtering the nearest neighbors

questions.explanation: With post-filtering, the top-k neighbors are found first and then filtered, which can leave too few results. Pre-filtering narrows the candidate set first, so k results can still be returned.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: Retrieved chunks from long technical manuals lose their section context, so the model cannot tell which product a passage refers to. Which ingestion approach helps most?

options.A: Chunk every 200 characters without regard to headings, since smaller chunks always retain more context than larger ones
options.B: Use the layout-aware skill to chunk along Markdown headings and keep the section headers with each chunk
options.C: Index each manual as a single chunk, so that the model always sees the whole manual whichever passage matches
options.D: Remove all headings from the documents before indexing, so that only body text influences the embeddings

questions.explanation: Structure-aware chunking with section headers preserves the context that identifies a passage. Blind splitting or removing headings loses it, and whole-manual chunks dilute relevance and exceed limits.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: A skillset with OCR and embedding skills is slow and costly because a change to a late-stage skill triggers reprocessing of every document through all skills. What feature reduces this?

options.A: Delete the skillset and index every document again without any enrichment, since enrichment cannot be cached
options.B: Increase the number of replicas, which causes upstream skill outputs to be stored permanently at no cost
options.C: Disable the OCR skill for all documents, because it is the only skill that can ever cause reprocessing
options.D: Enable the indexer enrichment cache so unchanged upstream skill outputs are reused during incremental enrichment

questions.explanation: Incremental enrichment with a cache stores intermediate results so that only affected skills rerun, saving time and cost. Replicas or disabling OCR do not provide reuse.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: A search index needs a change that cannot be applied in place, such as a new analyzer, and the application must stay available. Which technique gives a zero-downtime switch?

options.A: Rename the current index to a temporary name and hope that the client applications discover the new name
options.B: Build a new index in parallel and move an index alias to it once it is populated and validated
options.C: Delete the existing index during business hours and rebuild it while users wait for the results
options.D: Add replicas to the current index until it accepts the new analyzer without needing to be rebuilt

questions.explanation: Aliases let applications refer to a stable name, so a rebuilt index can be swapped in without client changes or downtime. Deleting, renaming or adding replicas does not solve the change safely.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: Users ask complex, multi-part questions such as "compare the refund and warranty terms for products A and B", and a single query retrieves only part of the needed evidence. Which Azure AI Search capability targets this?

options.A: Agentic retrieval, which uses a model to break the question into focused subqueries, runs them in parallel and merges the results
options.B: A lower vector dimension, which makes the single query embedding cover more topics with the same vector
options.C: A scoring profile that boosts the word "compare", so that comparison documents rise to the top of the results
options.D: A larger replica count, which lets a single query search deeper into each product's documents at once

questions.explanation: Complex questions benefit from decomposition into subqueries whose results are combined. Capacity, boosting one word or shrinking vectors does not add coverage of multiple sub-questions.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: A billion-vector index is expensive to store. Which combination lowers storage while preserving most quality?

options.A: Store the same vectors in two fields so that queries can use whichever copy happens to be cheaper to read
options.B: Drop random dimensions from each vector at index time, and then use the same shortened vectors for every query
options.C: Switch from vectors to alphabetical sorting, because sorting by title costs less than similarity search
options.D: Use vector compression such as scalar or binary quantization with oversampling, and rescore candidates using the original vectors

questions.explanation: Quantization reduces per-vector storage, and oversampling with rescoring on originals recovers accuracy. Randomly dropping dimensions harms quality, and duplicating vectors increases storage.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: A hybrid pipeline uses the semantic ranker, but answers ignore relevant text found late in long chunks. What is the most likely reason and fix?

options.A: The ranker discards the first half of every chunk, so chunks should be placed in the reverse order before indexing
options.B: The ranker only works on titles, so the content field should be renamed to title to make it visible to the ranker
options.C: The ranker reads a limited amount of each document and reranks only top candidates, so keep chunks concise and retrieve enough candidates
options.D: The semantic ranker reads every chunk in full regardless of length, so the problem must be the model's temperature setting

questions.explanation: Semantic reranking applies to a bounded set of first-stage results and a limited portion of each document, so overlong chunks lose their tail. Right-sized chunks and enough candidates address it.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: Documents contain customer PII, and policy requires it to be masked before content is indexed and embedded. Which approach fits an Azure AI Search pipeline?

options.A: Ask the model to forget any PII that appears in the retrieved passages at the moment it writes an answer
options.B: Index the raw text first and rely on a content filter to hide PII from users at answer time
options.C: Encrypt the search service with a customer-managed key, which removes PII from every document that is stored
options.D: Add the PII detection skill to the skillset and index the masked text, so raw PII never reaches the index or the embeddings

questions.explanation: Masking during enrichment keeps PII out of both the searchable text and the vectors. Output filtering or encryption leaves the data in the index, and models cannot be told to forget it.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A RAG chatbot summarizes web pages, and one page contains hidden text telling the assistant to reveal internal data. Which combination provides the best defense in depth?

options.A: Increase the model temperature so that the assistant is less likely to follow any instruction that appears in the text
options.B: Remove the content filter, because it might be the component that lets hidden instructions through to the model
options.C: Apply Prompt Shields to prompts and documents, use spotlighting on untrusted text, and limit assistant privileges
options.D: Add a sentence to the system message asking the model to ignore hidden text, and consider the risk to be solved

questions.explanation: Document attack detection, marking untrusted text and constraining privileges together reduce indirect injection. A single sentence in the prompt is not reliable, and sampling or removing filters does not help.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A RAG application must never show an answer that is unsupported by the retrieved passages. Which step best enforces this before the answer reaches users?

options.A: Lower the temperature to zero, which prevents the model from ever stating anything that is not in the passages
options.B: Send the response and its sources to groundedness detection, and return a fallback when the answer is ungrounded
options.C: Ask the model at the end of its answer whether it is confident, and display the answer when the model says yes
options.D: Increase the number of retrieved passages until the model no longer needs to use any knowledge of its own

questions.explanation: A separate groundedness check gives an objective gate on unsupported claims. Model self-reports, more passages and low temperature reduce but do not guarantee grounding.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A financial firm needs to detect content that is specific to its policies, such as improper investment promises, which the standard harm categories do not cover. What should it use?

options.A: Custom categories in Azure AI Content Safety, defined and trained with examples of the content to detect
options.B: The image analysis API, since improper promises can only appear inside pictures rather than in text
options.C: The hate category at its lowest severity setting, because improper promises are a form of hateful speech
options.D: A blocklist of every word in the dictionary, so that no undesired phrase can ever pass through the filter

questions.explanation: Custom categories let teams define organization-specific content classes with examples. Standard categories are for a fixed set of harms, and a dictionary blocklist would block everything.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Security operations wants to detect and investigate jailbreak attempts against a production Azure OpenAI application. Which measure best supports this?

options.A: Enable Defender for Cloud AI threat protection and pass end-user context so alerts correlate to users
options.B: Disable all logging to reduce the amount of data that analysts have to review each morning
options.C: Rely only on the model to detect its own jailbreaks and report them to the security team by email
options.D: Add a public web page that lists the prompts that were blocked, so the internet can help identify attackers

questions.explanation: AI threat protection surfaces attacks such as jailbreaks, and end-user context makes alerts actionable. Disabling logs or relying on the model for self-reporting removes visibility.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A single-page web app calls Azure OpenAI directly from the browser using an API key embedded in the JavaScript bundle. What is the correct remediation?

options.A: Restrict the key to a shorter time period, and publish the new key in the bundle every day after rotation
options.B: Move the key into a browser cookie, since cookies are hidden from the code that runs in the page
options.C: Route calls through a backend that uses managed identity, and remove and rotate the exposed key
options.D: Obfuscate the JavaScript so that the key cannot be read easily and continue using key-based calls from the browser

questions.explanation: Anything shipped to a browser can be extracted, so secrets must stay on a backend that uses Entra-based authentication. Obfuscation, daily publication or cookies do not protect the key.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Before releasing a new AI feature in a sensitive domain, a company wants a structured way to identify affected stakeholders, potential harms and mitigations. Which practice fits Microsoft's Responsible AI guidance?

options.A: Limit the assessment to the security team, since responsible AI concerns are only about network vulnerabilities
options.B: Complete a Responsible AI impact assessment early, document the harms and mitigations, and revisit it as the system changes
options.C: Ask the model to write its own risk assessment and accept it without review by any person
options.D: Publish the feature first and wait for user complaints to identify which harms actually occurred

questions.explanation: An impact assessment makes harms and mitigations explicit before release and evolves with the system. Waiting for complaints, unreviewed model output or a security-only view misses affected groups.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Diagnostic logs for an Azure OpenAI application in a Log Analytics workspace may contain personal data from prompts. Which measures best reduce risk while keeping observability?

options.A: Give every employee reader access to the workspace so that anyone can investigate incidents without requesting permission
options.B: Restrict workspace access with RBAC, set retention limits, and mask or drop sensitive fields with data collection transformations
options.C: Retain the logs indefinitely so that no evidence is ever lost, even when the data is no longer needed
options.D: Export the logs to a public storage container so that external auditors can download them without credentials

questions.explanation: Sensitive logs need least-privilege access, retention limits and minimization. Broad access, unlimited retention or public exposure increase the risk.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A healthcare customer objects that Azure OpenAI may retain prompts and completions for abuse monitoring, and its policies forbid any human review of patient-related text. What is the appropriate step?

options.A: Add a blocklist term for every patient name, which prevents the service from keeping any prompt that mentions them
options.B: Assume prompts are never stored anywhere, since abuse monitoring is a feature that is limited to the free trial tier only
options.C: Ask the model in the system message not to log anything, so that the platform stops retaining the conversation data
options.D: Review the retention and abuse monitoring terms, and apply for modified abuse monitoring if eligible

questions.explanation: Default abuse monitoring can retain prompts and completions for a limited time for review, and eligible customers can apply for modified abuse monitoring. Prompts and blocklists cannot change platform retention.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: An API on Azure Functions (Consumption plan) shows occasional multi-second delays on the first request after idle periods, which breaks a latency target for a chat feature. What is the best fix?

options.A: Move the function to a smaller region, because low traffic Regions never have cold starts for any workload
options.B: Use always-ready or pre-warmed instances, such as Flex Consumption always-ready or a Premium plan
options.C: Remove Application Insights, since telemetry collection is the only cause of a delay after periods of inactivity
options.D: Increase the model's max_completion_tokens so the function stays busy and never becomes idle between requests

questions.explanation: Cold starts occur when instances are scaled to zero, so keeping instances warm addresses them. Token limits, removing telemetry or changing Region do not eliminate cold starts.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: A team frequently changes prompts and retrieval settings and wants to stop regressions before deployment. Which CI/CD practice is most effective?

options.A: Deploy every change directly to production and rely on user complaints as the only source of quality data
options.B: Freeze all prompts permanently and forbid any change, so that no regression can ever be introduced again
options.C: Merge changes when at least one developer thinks the answers to a few sample questions look better than before
options.D: Run Foundry evaluations on a golden dataset in the pipeline and fail the build below agreed thresholds

questions.explanation: Automated evaluation gates catch quality and safety regressions early with objective thresholds. Informal checks or complaint-driven feedback are slow and subjective, and freezing prompts blocks improvement.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Offline evaluations pass, but production quality drifts over weeks as user questions change. Which capability provides ongoing detection?

options.A: A manual review of the first ten conversations every year, along with a note in the release checklist
options.B: A single evaluation run before launch, since offline results are certain to remain valid however the traffic changes
options.C: Continuous evaluation that samples production traces, runs evaluators on them, and raises Azure Monitor alerts when scores decline
options.D: A higher temperature value so that the model adapts automatically to new kinds of user questions

questions.explanation: Production traffic evolves, so sampling live interactions and scoring them continuously reveals drift that pre-release tests cannot. One-off or rare reviews miss it, and temperature does not adapt a model.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: A business-critical RAG application must survive the loss of a Region with a modest recovery time. Azure AI Search does not replicate an index across Regions by itself. Which design fits?

options.A: Store the index definition in a spreadsheet and rebuild it manually after an outage has been resolved by the cloud provider
options.B: Back up the model deployment only, since the search index can be recreated by the users when they next visit
options.C: Run a second search service in another Region populated by the same indexers or pipeline, and route traffic with Front Door or API Management
options.D: Rely on a single search service with more replicas, since replicas automatically copy the index into other Regions

questions.explanation: Search replicas are within one service and Region, so cross-Region resilience needs a secondary service kept in sync and a routing layer. Manual rebuilds or model-only backups extend recovery time.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Development experiments repeatedly consume the tokens-per-minute quota for a model in a Region, and production requests get throttled. What is the most robust remedy?

options.A: Increase the max_completion_tokens in production, which reserves more of the shared quota for production requests
options.B: Place production in a dedicated subscription or resource with its own quota allocation, and keep development in separate ones
options.C: Ask developers to run their experiments only at night, since quota limits do not apply between midnight and 6 AM
options.D: Rename the production deployment so that the platform prioritizes it above every other deployment for the model

questions.explanation: Quota is granted per subscription, Region and model, so isolating production gives it dedicated capacity. Time-of-day habits, token limits or deployment names do not reserve quota.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: A workload has run at a steady, high volume on provisioned throughput for months and is expected to continue for a year. How can the team lower cost further?

options.A: Purchase an Azure reservation for provisioned throughput, committing for a term in exchange for a discount
options.B: Switch to smaller prompts by removing the system message, which changes the price of every provisioned unit
options.C: Delete and recreate the deployment each month, because new deployments are always billed at a lower rate
options.D: Move all traffic to a different Region every week to take advantage of the daily price differences between Regions

questions.explanation: Committed reservations reduce the price of steady provisioned capacity. The other actions do not change the unit price and may harm stability.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: A client of Azure OpenAI experiences bursts of 429 responses even though it retries. The team wants smarter behavior across two deployments in different Regions. Which combination is best?

options.A: Send every request to both deployments and use whichever answer arrives first, discarding the slower response
options.B: Ignore the rate limit headers and send more requests concurrently, so that the service finishes them sooner
options.C: Increase the client timeout to several hours so that throttled requests are never abandoned by the caller
options.D: Pace requests using rate limit headers, and fail over with an APIM backend pool and circuit breaker

questions.explanation: Headers tell clients how much capacity remains, and a gateway with a circuit breaker routes around throttled backends. Doubling requests or waiting hours worsens load or delays users.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Different teams instrument their Azure OpenAI apps differently, making it hard to compare token usage and latency across applications. Which practice solves this?

options.A: Disable telemetry in all applications and rely on the invoice to determine how each application performed
options.B: Log only the final text answers, since token counts and latencies can always be estimated from the length of the text
options.C: Adopt the OpenTelemetry generative AI semantic conventions so spans and metrics use consistent names and attributes
options.D: Let each team invent its own metric names, and merge the dashboards by hand at the end of every month

questions.explanation: Standard semantic conventions yield uniform, comparable telemetry for token usage, latency and model details across services. Ad hoc names, text-only logs or no telemetry hinder analysis.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A regulated EU workload needs both predictable latency and processing kept inside the EU geography. Which deployment type combination fits best?

options.A: A Data Zone Provisioned deployment for the EU, which reserves capacity while keeping processing inside the zone
options.B: A Global Provisioned deployment, which reserves capacity but may process requests in any Region around the world
options.C: A Standard deployment in a non-EU Region, with a contract clause stating that the data must remain in the EU
options.D: A Global Standard deployment, which pools capacity worldwide and may process requests in any Region with room

questions.explanation: Data Zone Provisioned combines reserved throughput with a defined geography for processing. Global deployment types can process outside the zone, and a contract clause does not change where processing happens.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A team proposes using the model router for every request in a regulated workflow that must be validated against a single certified model version. What is the main concern?

options.A: The router removes all content filtering from requests, which is not acceptable in regulated environments
options.B: The router can only forward requests to embedding models, so it is unsuitable for any chat workflow
options.C: The router permanently locks the deployment to the most expensive model, which makes validation impossible
options.D: The router may pick different models over time, so behavior may not match the one validated version

questions.explanation: Routing across models improves cost and quality but trades away determinism about which model answered. Workflows that need a fixed validated model should deploy that model directly.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: An agent tool needs a third-party API key. Which storage and access pattern is best?

options.A: Store the key in a public blob container with a long random name, and let the application download it when it starts
options.B: Store the key in the agent's instructions so that the model can attach it to each tool call that it makes
options.C: Store the key in Azure Key Vault, grant the app's managed identity the Key Vault Secrets User role, and reference the secret at runtime
options.D: Store the key in the application's source repository in a settings file, and restrict the repository to the development team

questions.explanation: Key Vault with managed identity and RBAC keeps secrets out of code and prompts and supports rotation and auditing. Source files, prompts and obscure public URLs expose the key.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A Foundry hub must prevent agents and notebooks from sending data to arbitrary internet destinations, while still reaching approved services. Which networking approach fits?

options.A: Assign public IP addresses to each compute resource, so that outbound traffic can be traced by address after an incident
options.B: Block all outbound traffic, including traffic to the approved storage and model endpoints that the workloads depend on
options.C: Allow all outbound internet traffic, and rely on developers to avoid connecting to unapproved destinations
options.D: Use a managed virtual network in an approved-outbound-only mode, with private endpoints or outbound rules for the approved destinations

questions.explanation: Restricting outbound access to an approved list controls exfiltration paths while keeping required services reachable. Open outbound or a total block, or tracing by IP afterward, fails on control or usability.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: The security team wants to ensure that only approved models can be deployed to any Azure OpenAI resource in the subscription, including by mistake in the portal. What is the best mechanism?

options.A: A wiki page that lists approved models, which developers are asked to read before they deploy anything
options.B: An Azure Advisor recommendation that appears in the portal when someone deploys an unapproved model
options.C: A custom Azure Policy with a deny effect that restricts deployments to an approved list of models
options.D: A budget alert that is triggered when the cost of an unapproved model exceeds the monthly limit

questions.explanation: Policy with deny is a preventive control enforced at deployment time. Documentation, advice and budget alerts do not stop unapproved deployments from being created.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: AI Search index definitions, skillsets and indexers were created by hand in the portal, and a Region rebuild after an incident takes days because nobody remembers the exact settings. What is the best remedy?

options.A: Take periodic screenshots of the portal pages so that engineers can retype the settings during a rebuild
options.B: Keep the definitions as versioned code, such as JSON or Bicep, and deploy them through a pipeline
options.C: Disable indexers permanently, and re-upload every document manually whenever users report that results are missing
options.D: Ask the original developer to remember the settings, and record them in a chat message for later reference

questions.explanation: Configuration as code makes search resources reproducible, reviewable and quick to redeploy. Screenshots, memory or manual re-uploads are slow and error-prone.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A client application hard-codes the Azure OpenAI deployment name, and a team wants to move to a newer model without changing every client. Which practice makes this easier?

options.A: Embed the model version in the deployment name and require every client to be recompiled at each upgrade
options.B: Create a new Azure OpenAI resource for each model version, and give clients a new endpoint every time
options.C: Rename the deployment each time the model changes and email all client owners to update the name in their code
options.D: Use stable, logical deployment names and update the model or version behind them, testing first, so clients keep the same name

questions.explanation: Clients call deployments by name, so a stable name decouples them from the model behind it. Renaming or new resources per version force coordinated client changes.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: An organization keeps API keys for Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search in Foundry connections. Which change improves security the most?

options.A: Share the connection keys with all project members so that nobody needs to request access to them
options.B: Rotate the keys once every five years, because frequent rotation causes outages for the applications that use them
options.C: Use Microsoft Entra ID-based connections that rely on managed identity and RBAC, and disable key-based authentication where supported
options.D: Store the connection keys in the project description field, so that they are easy to find and copy

questions.explanation: Identity-based access removes long-lived secrets and enables auditing and least privilege. Sharing, exposing or rarely rotating keys increases the risk of misuse.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A function-calling flow often receives arguments with wrong types or unexpected enum values. Which combination most improves reliability?

options.A: Describe the function in one vague sentence, and trust the model to guess the argument names and types it should supply
options.B: Remove the parameter schema from the definition so that the model has more freedom in how it formats the arguments
options.C: Increase the temperature so that the model tries more argument combinations until one of them happens to be accepted
options.D: Define strict parameter schemas with enums and clear descriptions, enable strict mode on the function, and still validate arguments in code

questions.explanation: Precise schemas and strict mode constrain the model's arguments, and server-side validation is the final safeguard. Vague definitions, randomness or removing the schema make errors more likely.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A healthcare app uses the Responses API in stateful mode, but privacy rules say conversation content must not be retained by the service beyond the request. What should the developers do?

options.A: Turn on the seed parameter, since a fixed seed causes the service to discard the conversation after each response
options.B: Set the temperature to zero, because deterministic responses are never stored by the service after being returned
options.C: Disable response storage where supported, and manage conversation history within the application instead of relying on stored state
options.D: Keep response storage on and simply tell users that their conversation is retained for later reference

questions.explanation: Stateful features rely on stored responses, so privacy constraints may require disabling storage and handling context yourself. Seeds and temperature do not control retention.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A vision workflow classifies thousands of product photos into coarse categories, and token costs are high. Which adjustment reduces cost without much quality loss?

options.A: Convert every image into a very long text description by hand before sending, so the model receives no images at all
options.B: Send each image four times so that the model can average its answers, which lowers the overall token count
options.C: Always use the highest detail setting, since it is guaranteed to reduce the number of tokens used for each image
options.D: Use the low detail setting for images where fine text and small features are not needed, and reserve high detail for images that require it

questions.explanation: Image detail affects token usage, so coarse tasks can use low detail while fine-grained tasks need high detail. Repeating requests or manual conversion increases cost or effort.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A team fine-tunes a smaller model using outputs from a larger one and needs to prove that the smaller model is acceptable. Which practice provides that evidence?

options.A: Compare the models only by the length of their answers, since longer answers always indicate better quality
options.B: Assume that the smaller model matches the larger one because it was trained on the larger model's outputs
options.C: Test the smaller model on the same examples that were used in training, and report that it scores perfectly
options.D: Evaluate both models on a held-out test set with agreed metrics, and compare quality, cost and latency before switching

questions.explanation: Held-out evaluation with defined metrics shows real generalization, whereas testing on training data or comparing lengths hides quality gaps.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A schema used with strict structured outputs keeps being rejected. It has optional fields and allows additional properties. What is the likely fix?

options.A: Remove the schema completely and ask for JSON in the prompt, since strict mode accepts any schema that is provided
options.B: Add more optional fields and allow additional properties, so the schema is flexible enough for strict mode
options.C: Change the schema to use a list of strings only, because strict mode does not support objects of any kind
options.D: Mark every field as required, set additionalProperties to false, and represent optional values as nullable types

questions.explanation: Strict structured outputs support a subset of JSON Schema in which all fields are required and extra properties are disallowed, with optional values expressed as nullable. Loosening the schema makes it less compatible.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: The same prompt with a fixed seed and temperature zero sometimes gives slightly different answers on different days. Which response field can help explain this?

options.A: system_fingerprint, which changes with backend configuration and can explain differences despite the same seed
options.B: The HTTP status code, which is different for every request and identifies the answer that was returned
options.C: The model's display name, which changes every day and makes each answer different from the previous one
options.D: The Azure subscription ID, which the service uses as an additional random seed for each call

questions.explanation: Determinism is best effort, and backend changes can alter output. Comparing system_fingerprint values helps identify such changes, whereas the other fields do not relate to sampling.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A team's prompts to an o-series model still use a system message, and the model seems to ignore some of the intended instructions. What should they check?

options.A: Whether the model expects a developer message instead of a system message, and update the prompt roles as recommended for reasoning models
options.B: Whether the temperature is high enough, since reasoning models follow instructions only when they are given a temperature above one
options.C: Whether the system message contains capital letters, since reasoning models treat capitalized words as commands to skip
options.D: Whether the system message is longer than ten words, since reasoning models ignore any message that is longer than that

questions.explanation: Reasoning models use the developer role to carry instructions, replacing the system role used by earlier chat models. Prompt length, temperature or capitalization are not the cause.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A Semantic Kernel agent can call plugins that send emails and delete records automatically. The business wants approval and logging before sensitive functions run. Which feature helps?

options.A: Running the plugins on the same thread as the model, which lets them share approval decisions without any configuration
options.B: Deleting the function descriptions, since a model can only call a function when it has a description to read
options.C: Function invocation filters, which intercept calls to require approval, log them, or block them before the function executes
options.D: A higher temperature, which makes the model less likely to call sensitive functions during a conversation

questions.explanation: Filters let the application intercept function calls for policy checks, approvals and audit logging. Sampling settings and removing descriptions do not enforce control.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: A classifier built on a chat model returns a label, but downstream systems need to know how confident the model is so they can route uncertain cases to a person. Which technique helps?

options.A: Increase the max_completion_tokens so that longer answers imply higher confidence in the chosen label
options.B: Send the same prompt with a different system message and assume the answer with the longer text is more confident
options.C: Request logprobs and derive a confidence score from the probability of the label tokens, then set a threshold for human review
options.D: Ask the model to append the word "certain" to every answer, and treat every answer that has it as fully reliable

questions.explanation: Token log probabilities expose how strongly the model favored a label, enabling calibrated thresholds. Self-declared certainty, length or system message variations are not reliable confidence signals.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: An agent with 60 registered tools frequently picks the wrong one and is slow to respond. Which redesign is most effective?

options.A: Expose fewer tools per agent by specializing agents or filtering tools by context, and sharpen descriptions
options.B: Increase the temperature so that the model explores different tools at random until one of them succeeds
options.C: Add ten more tools that overlap with the existing ones, so that the model has more chances to pick a suitable one
options.D: Shorten all tool descriptions to a single word so that the model does not have to read long descriptions

questions.explanation: Selection accuracy drops with many similar tools. Narrowing the set per agent and writing clear descriptions helps, while more overlap, terse descriptions or randomness worsen it.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: A company has agents built with different frameworks in different teams, and wants them to collaborate without rewriting them. Which approach fits?

options.A: Rewrite every agent in the same programming language and framework before any collaboration is attempted
options.B: Have the agents exchange information by writing to a shared text file that all of them poll every few seconds
options.C: Use an open agent-to-agent protocol such as A2A so that agents can discover each other and exchange tasks across frameworks
options.D: Merge all agents into a single prompt with all of their instructions, and let one model play every role

questions.explanation: Standard interoperability protocols let heterogeneous agents interact without rewrites. Forced rewrites, polling files or one giant prompt sacrifice modularity and reliability.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: Auditors ask which agent performed which action on which data. Several agents currently share one service principal. What design change addresses this?

options.A: Disable audit logging for the agents, since auditors only need to see the final results that users receive
options.B: Keep the shared service principal and ask the agents to write their names in the log messages they create
options.C: Give each agent its own managed or agent identity with minimum permissions so logs attribute actions per agent
options.D: Use the subscription owner account for all agents so that every action is recorded under one well-known name

questions.explanation: Distinct identities allow accurate attribution and least privilege per agent. Self-reported names in logs are unreliable, and shared or owner accounts obscure accountability.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: An expense approval process has five fixed steps with compliance sign-offs, and the team is debating a fully autonomous agent versus another design. Which is more appropriate?

options.A: A single prompt that asks the model to pretend it has completed all five steps and report that they were done
options.B: A manual spreadsheet process, because no automated design can meet compliance requirements involving several steps
options.C: A fully autonomous agent that decides its own steps each time, since flexibility is always preferable to predictability
options.D: A deterministic workflow, such as Logic Apps or an agent framework workflow, that uses a model only for steps that need language understanding

questions.explanation: Fixed, auditable processes benefit from deterministic orchestration with model calls used where needed. Autonomy adds unpredictability, and pretend steps or manual-only approaches do not satisfy the need.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: A support agent repeatedly fails to resolve a billing dispute and keeps apologizing. What is the best design for such cases?

options.A: Let the agent continue indefinitely until the customer gives up, since ending the conversation early looks bad
options.B: Hide the failure from the customer and mark the ticket as resolved, so that the metrics remain high
options.C: Increase the max tokens so that the agent's apologies become longer and more convincing to the customer
options.D: Define escalation triggers, such as low confidence or repeated tool failures, that hand off to a person with context

questions.explanation: Human handoff on defined triggers keeps hard cases from stalling and preserves context. Endless loops, misreporting or longer apologies harm customers and data quality.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: A long-running agent thread grows until requests become slow and expensive. Which run setting helps control this while keeping recent context?

options.A: Adding a large amount of filler text to each message so that older messages are pushed out sooner
options.B: A truncation strategy that keeps only the last N messages in the model's context for each run
options.C: Deleting the agent and creating a new one after every message, so that the previous history is always lost
options.D: Setting the temperature to zero so that the thread stops adding messages to its history

questions.explanation: Truncation strategies bound how much history is sent to the model on each run, limiting cost and latency. Sampling changes or deleting the agent do not manage context sensibly.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: A team needs to test its agent against many realistic and adversarial multi-turn conversations before launch, without recruiting hundreds of testers. What helps?

options.A: Use simulators for synthetic multi-turn and adversarial conversations, and score them with evaluators
options.B: Wait until launch and collect conversations from real customers, then fix problems as complaints arrive
options.C: Test only the model without tools, because tool behavior is never part of the risk of an agent
options.D: Ask the agent's developers to try five or six friendly questions and declare the agent ready for launch

questions.explanation: Simulated conversations scale coverage of normal and hostile scenarios before release, and evaluators score outcomes. Friendly spot checks, post-launch discovery or ignoring tools leave large gaps.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: A pricing agent occasionally spins for many minutes, calling tools repeatedly and burning tokens. Which control gives the most direct protection?

options.A: Ask the agent in its instructions to try to be quick, and treat the request as a limit on its behavior
options.B: Enforce step, time and token budgets per run, and stop or escalate when they are exceeded
options.C: Raise the temperature, so that the agent chooses different actions and eventually finishes on its own
options.D: Remove the logging of tool calls, so that the agent no longer has to spend time writing entries

questions.explanation: Hard budgets bound the worst case regardless of model behavior. Sampling changes, removing logs and polite requests do not guarantee termination.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: In a hybrid query with the semantic ranker, results improve when the first stage returns more candidates. Which query parameters should the team adjust?

options.A: Increase only the number of replicas, because more replicas return more candidates for every single query
options.B: Increase k for the vector query and top for text results so the ranker has enough candidates to rerank
options.C: Turn off the vector query, because reranking can only be applied to the results from a keyword search
options.D: Set both k and top to one, because reranking works best when it sees only one candidate

questions.explanation: Reranking can only reorder what the first stage returns, so retrieving a wider candidate set gives it material to work with. Capacity changes do not alter the result count.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: A team wants to move from text-embedding-ada-002 to text-embedding-3-large without downtime. Which migration approach is sound?

options.A: Add a new vector field, backfill it with new embeddings, switch queries to the new field once validated, and then remove the old field
options.B: Keep the old field and only embed new documents with the new model, mixing both types of vectors in the same field
options.C: Overwrite the vectors in the existing field with new ones gradually, while queries still use the old embedding model
options.D: Change the embedding model name in the query only and leave the stored vectors untouched, since embeddings are compatible

questions.explanation: Vectors from different models are not comparable, so a parallel field lets you backfill and cut over safely. Mixing or partially updating a field yields inconsistent similarity results.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: A catalog document has both a title and long description. Users often search by short titles, and sometimes by concepts in descriptions. Which index design supports both well?

options.A: Store only the description and discard titles, since descriptions always contain the same words as the titles
options.B: Store only the title and discard descriptions, since short titles are the only text that users ever type
options.C: Use separate vector fields for the title and the description, and query them together with weights or as multiple vector queries
options.D: Combine title and description into one long string with no separation, and use only a single vector for all queries

questions.explanation: Separate fields let the query target short-title and long-description semantics differently, and multiple vector queries can be combined. One blended vector or discarding content loses that precision.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: Source documents in SharePoint have user-level permissions, and the RAG application must respect them. Which approach preserves access control?

options.A: Give every user the same broad access to the index, since users will only ask about documents that they are allowed to read
options.B: Index all documents without permission data, and add a line to the prompt asking the model not to reveal restricted text
options.C: Copy each document into a public container so that permission checks are not needed for any of the users
options.D: Ingest permission metadata such as ACLs or group IDs with each document and filter results at query time using the caller's identity

questions.explanation: Permission-aware retrieval requires ACL data in the index and enforcement in the query. Prompts and honor systems do not stop the retrieval of restricted content.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: An analytics team wants to run reports over the enriched output of an indexing pipeline, such as extracted entities and key phrases, separate from search. Which feature fits?

options.A: A synonym map, which keeps a copy of every entity extracted by the skillset in the application logs
options.B: A semantic configuration, which stores the enriched entities in the query logs for later export
options.C: A knowledge store, which projects enriched content into Azure Storage as tables, objects or files for downstream analysis
options.D: A scoring profile, which exports the enriched content into a spreadsheet each time a user runs a search

questions.explanation: Knowledge store persists enrichment output outside the index for analytics or downstream processing. Scoring profiles, semantic configurations and synonym maps affect retrieval, not persistence.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: In a hybrid search, the vector branch matches concepts well, but the keyword branch dominates results for queries that have many common words. What can the team do to influence the fusion?

options.A: Sort the results alphabetically after fusion, so that both branches contribute the same amount to the final list
options.B: Adjust the weights of the vector and text queries so that the fused ranking gives more influence to the vector branch
options.C: Increase the number of partitions, which lets the vector branch carry more influence during the fusion of the ranked lists
options.D: Delete the keyword index, because fusion cannot work unless one branch has no content

questions.explanation: Queries can assign relative weights that affect how much each branch contributes in fusion. Deleting a branch or changing partitions does not tune contribution.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: Users search for "PTO" but the documents use "paid time off" and "vacation", so relevant results are missed by keyword queries. Which feature fixes this cheaply?

options.A: A lower embedding dimension, because shorter vectors treat similar words as identical in keyword search
options.B: A larger partition count, which makes the engine read more words in every document
options.C: A synonym map that links the equivalent terms, applied to the searchable fields
options.D: A higher temperature in the chat model, which makes it guess the abbreviations that users typed

questions.explanation: Synonym maps expand keyword queries to equivalent terms without changing the content. Capacity, embedding size or sampling do not influence keyword matching.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: A team debates using Azure Cosmos DB with vector search versus Azure AI Search for a retrieval workload. The data is operational, updated per transaction, and needs vector lookups next to the record. Which choice is more suitable?

options.A: Azure Blob Storage only, because blobs can run similarity queries directly on the files stored inside them
options.B: Azure AI Search only, because it is the sole Azure service that can store an embedding next to another value
options.C: Cosmos DB with vector search, co-locating vectors with transactional data, unless rich search features are needed
options.D: Azure DNS, because DNS records can store embeddings and return nearest neighbors for a query

questions.explanation: Operational data with vectors can live in a database that supports vector search, while Azure AI Search adds richer retrieval features. Blob Storage and DNS do not perform similarity search.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: A RAG index is built from PDFs whose scanned pages include tables with merged cells, and simple OCR outputs jumbled text. Which change most improves the extracted structure?

options.A: Increase the OCR font size setting, because larger characters cause the tables to be recognized as tables
options.B: Use Document Intelligence layout analysis, which extracts tables and reading order, and chunk from its structured Markdown output
options.C: Convert every PDF to an image thumbnail and index the thumbnail file names instead of the content
options.D: Use a text split skill on the raw OCR output, since splitting text always repairs the jumbled table structure

questions.explanation: Layout analysis understands tables and reading order, which OCR alone lacks. Splitting jumbled text or indexing thumbnails cannot recover structure.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A regulated team must encrypt Azure OpenAI data with a customer-managed key. Which prerequisite and permission does the key setup require?

options.A: A storage account key pasted into the Azure OpenAI resource settings, replacing the Key Vault entirely
