options.B: A Key Vault with soft delete and purge protection, and an identity authorized to use the key
options.C: A Key Vault with soft delete disabled, and an identity that has no permission on the key
options.D: A public GitHub repository that contains the key material, so the service can read it when needed

questions.explanation: Customer-managed keys need a protected Key Vault and an identity authorized to use the key. Disabling protections, omitting permissions or publishing keys defeats the control.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A workflow sends customer messages to a model, but policy says real names and account numbers must never reach it, though the answer must still address the customer by name. What is a good design?

options.A: Ask the model to guess the customer's name, so that no real identifier needs to be sent or stored
options.B: Replace identifiers with placeholders before the call, keep a secure mapping, and restore the real values in the response afterward
options.C: Remove the customer's name from the final answer, so that the response is never personalized at all
options.D: Send the raw messages, because the model provider is bound to delete all personal data immediately after each request

questions.explanation: Reversible masking keeps sensitive values out of the model while preserving personalization. Sending raw data violates policy, and dropping or guessing names harms the experience or accuracy.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: After an AI Red Teaming Agent run, the attack success rate for jailbreak prompts is higher than the release threshold. What is the correct next step?

options.A: Lower the release threshold until the current result passes, since the threshold is only a suggestion
options.B: Block the release, strengthen mitigations such as Prompt Shields and instruction hardening, and retest
options.C: Release anyway, and document the result as an accepted risk without any further action on the mitigations
options.D: Delete the failing test prompts from the suite, so that the attack success rate falls below the threshold

questions.explanation: A gate exists to stop releases that exceed the agreed risk. Mitigating and retesting is the honest response, whereas removing tests or moving the threshold hides the problem.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A consumer platform uses Azure AI Content Safety to moderate posts. Some posts score at borderline severity, and both automatic blocking and automatic approval create errors. What is the better design?

options.A: Randomly decide each borderline post with a coin flip, so that errors are evenly distributed among users
options.B: Auto-block everything with any severity above zero, and ignore the appeals that users submit afterward
options.C: Auto-approve everything with a severity above zero, since the cost of a person reviewing content is always too high
options.D: Auto-block high severity, auto-allow low, and send the borderline range to human review that tunes thresholds

questions.explanation: Tiered handling places human judgment where automation is least certain, and the feedback improves thresholds. Blanket rules or randomness produce avoidable errors.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A user invokes the right to erasure. Their data may exist in chat threads, a vector index, application logs and fine-tuning files. What practice makes compliance realistic?

options.A: Keep a data inventory of where user data can reside and run a deletion or anonymization procedure for each store
options.B: Delete only the user's account record, and assume that the copies in other stores will be removed automatically
options.C: Wait for the retention period of every store to expire, even if it is several years, without taking any action
options.D: Tell the user that data used by AI systems cannot be deleted because models never forget anything

questions.explanation: Deletion requires knowing every place the data lands and having a procedure for each. Deleting one record or refusing does not satisfy the request.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Azure AI Search needs to call an Azure OpenAI embedding deployment to vectorize queries and documents, and the team wants no keys stored in the search service. What is the right setup?

options.A: Enable a managed identity on the search service and assign it the Cognitive Services OpenAI User role on the Azure OpenAI resource
options.B: Make the Azure OpenAI resource publicly writable, so that the search service does not need any credentials
options.C: Store the key in the index documents themselves, so that each document can authenticate the call on its own
options.D: Paste the Azure OpenAI key into the skillset definition, and give the search service the Owner role on the subscription

questions.explanation: Role-based access with the search service's managed identity avoids stored secrets and follows least privilege. Embedding keys in definitions or documents, or removing authentication, is insecure.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Both Azure AI Search and Azure OpenAI have public access disabled behind private endpoints, yet the search service's indexer and vectorizer cannot reach the OpenAI endpoint. What feature addresses this?

options.A: Re-enable public access on both resources permanently, since private connectivity from a search service is never supported
options.B: Turn off the vectorizer, since it can only work when the model is reachable from the internet
options.C: Add a public IP to each search replica, because replicas use their own address to reach the private endpoint
options.D: Create a shared private link from the search service to the Azure OpenAI resource, and approve the private endpoint connection

questions.explanation: Shared private links let managed search components reach other private resources without exposing them publicly. Re-enabling public access or adding public IPs defeats the isolation.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Administrators access the Foundry portal and manage model deployments from personal devices. Security wants stronger control for these privileged actions. Which measure helps most?

options.A: Remove multifactor authentication for administrators, so that emergency access is not delayed by extra steps
options.B: Allow sign-in from any device or location without extra checks, since administrators are trusted by default
options.C: Apply Conditional Access requiring MFA and compliant devices, plus just-in-time role elevation
options.D: Share a single administrator account with a strong password among all administrators to simplify auditing

questions.explanation: Conditional Access with MFA, device compliance and time-bound elevation reduces the risk of compromised privileged accounts. Shared accounts and removing checks increase it.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A public-facing assistant answers policy questions. Users may treat its answers as authoritative. Which Responsible AI practices best support transparency?

options.A: Present the answers as written by a human expert, so that users have more confidence in the information
options.B: Add a footer stating that the service is 100 percent accurate, so that the users stop double-checking its output
options.C: Disclose AI generation, cite sources, state limitations, and offer feedback or a route to a person
options.D: Hide the sources so users do not become confused, and offer no way to challenge the answers

questions.explanation: Transparency means clear AI disclosure, traceable sources, honest limits and a path to feedback or human help. Impersonation, hiding sources or false accuracy claims mislead users.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: A chat app hosted in one Region calls a model in another Region and an AI Search service in a third, and users complain about latency and egress charges. What is the first architectural fix?

options.A: Co-locate the app, the search service and the model deployment in the same or nearby Regions where allowed
options.B: Add more retries between the components, since retries always reduce the network latency of each request
options.C: Increase the model's max tokens, so that fewer round trips are needed between the Regions
options.D: Move each component to a different continent, so that the load is spread evenly across the internet

questions.explanation: Network distance adds latency and data transfer cost, so components that talk often should be placed close together. Retries and token limits do not shorten distance.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: A multi-tenant SaaS wants fair usage so that one tenant cannot consume all capacity of a shared Azure OpenAI deployment behind API Management. Which policy setup is best?

options.A: Rely on each tenant's honesty to keep their usage low, and review the invoice at the end of the month
options.B: Apply a token limit policy with a counter key based on the tenant identifier, and return remaining-token information to clients
options.C: Apply a single global request limit shared by all tenants, so the first tenant to reach it blocks everybody else
options.D: Give the busiest tenant the administrator subscription key, so its traffic is never throttled by any policy

questions.explanation: Per-tenant counters enforce fairness and isolate noisy neighbors, while a global counter penalizes everyone and honor systems or unlimited keys do not control capacity.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Before a launch, the team wants to know how the AI API behaves at 10 times the current traffic with realistic prompts. Which approach yields trustworthy results?

options.A: Skip load testing, because cloud services scale infinitely and never show throttling or latency growth
options.B: Test in a single-user development environment with the network cable unplugged, and multiply the result by ten
options.C: Run load tests, for example with Azure Load Testing, using realistic prompt sizes and concurrency
options.D: Send one request many times with an identical tiny prompt, since it shows the maximum possible throughput

questions.explanation: Realistic mixes of prompt lengths and concurrency reveal quota limits, latency growth and scaling behavior. Trivial repeated requests, unrealistic setups or assuming infinite scale do not.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: A team wants to change a prompt template or switch a model for 5 percent of users without redeploying code, and to roll back in seconds. Which approach fits?

options.A: Store the settings in the user's browser storage, so each user decides which prompt and model are used
options.B: Store prompt and model settings in Azure App Configuration with feature flags and change them at runtime
options.C: Hard-code the settings and redeploy the application for every change, which takes hours to complete
options.D: Email the new prompt to all users and ask them to paste it into the application themselves

questions.explanation: Runtime configuration with flags supports gradual exposure and instant rollback without a redeployment. Hard-coding, emailing prompts or user-controlled settings offer no safe control.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Documents are uploaded throughout the day and users expect them to be searchable within minutes, but a daily indexer schedule causes delays. Which design improves freshness while limiting cost?

options.A: Use Event Grid on new blobs to trigger a Function that runs the indexer, instead of polling on a long schedule
options.B: Ask users to email the search administrator whenever they upload a file so that indexing can be started
options.C: Keep the daily schedule and explain that uploaded documents are not searchable until the next day
options.D: Run the indexer every second around the clock, even when there are no new documents to process

questions.explanation: Event-driven triggers process documents as they arrive, achieving freshness without constant polling. Extremely frequent polling wastes resources, and manual or daily processes do not meet the requirement.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Full prompts and completions are logged to Log Analytics, and the monthly ingestion cost is now larger than the model bill. Which measures reduce cost while keeping useful observability?

options.A: Sample or truncate payloads, drop unneeded fields with transformations, and set table plan and retention
options.B: Turn off all diagnostics for the application, including metrics and traces that do not contain any payloads
options.C: Write each log entry to three different workspaces, so that at least one of them is inexpensive
options.D: Keep logging every field of every request forever, because the ingestion price does not depend on the volume of data

questions.explanation: Log cost follows volume and retention, so sampling, field filtering, table plan and retention align spend with need. Turning everything off or duplicating data removes visibility or increases cost.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: A nightly batch summarization job and a customer-facing chat feature share one deployment, and the batch job periodically causes chat timeouts. Which resilience pattern isolates them?

options.A: Use separate deployments per workload with independent limits, so one cannot exhaust the other's capacity
options.B: Ask chat users to retry their requests during the batch window, until the job has finished
options.C: Reduce the batch job to run once per month, whether or not the business still needs its output
options.D: Run both workloads through one queue with equal priority, so that a long batch job delays every chat request

questions.explanation: Bulkheads separate resource pools so failures or spikes in one workload do not spread. Shared queues, user retries or dropping the workload do not provide isolation.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: A chat backend occasionally receives context_length_exceeded errors when long conversations plus retrieved documents exceed the model's limit. What is the best prevention?

options.A: Wait for the error, and then retry the same oversized request until it succeeds without changing anything
options.B: Delete the system message every time the conversation becomes long, and add it back at the start of the next one
options.C: Count tokens locally before sending, and trim or summarize history and retrieved content to fit with headroom
options.D: Increase the temperature so that the service will accept longer prompts than the documented context limit

questions.explanation: Pre-counting tokens lets the application budget the context and shorten it before the call. Retrying unchanged or changing sampling cannot enlarge the window, and dropping the system message removes needed instructions.
